frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes DEMARCATION-BETWEEN: the positing of an interval/boundary separating two (or more) referents, and the DISTINCTNESS that this separation produces — one thing set apart from another so that it stands out as itself. The single residue has two co-present faces: (a) the separating interval ("between"), and (b) the distinctness/manifestness that follows from being set apart ("clear, evident, made-plain"). It is inherently dyadic (A demarcated from / against B).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes DEMARCATION-BETWEEN: the positing of an interval/boundary separating two (or more) referents, and the DISTINCTNESS that this separation produces — one thing set apart from another so that it stands out as itself. The single residue has two co-present faces: (a) the separating interval ("between"), and (b) the distinctness/manifestness that follows from being set apart ("clear, evident, made-plain"). It is inherently dyadic (A demarcated from / against B).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every occurrence turns on putting a gap or boundary between two things and thereby making them distinct. The 243 LOC uses (bayna, baynahum, bayna yadayhi, ma baynahuma) foreground the interval itself: 10:29 "between us and you", 15:85 "what is between them" (heavens and earth), 16:66 milk "from between dung and blood", 17:110 "between that" (a middle way), 18:61 the junction "between the two seas", 10:28 "we separated between them" (fazayyalna baynahum). The clarity cluster foregrounds the result of that separation: bayyinah/bayyinat (distinguishing proof, 83x N), bayyin/bayyinat (evident, 19x ADJ), mubin (manifest / that which makes distinct, Form IV, 119x across N(IV)+ADJ(IV)), bayyana (V-II, to set apart = make distinct/explain, 35x), tabayyana (V-V, to become distinct, or to seek the distinction/verify, 18x), abana/yubin (IV, 43:52 barely "makes himself plain" of Moses' speech), istabana/mustabin (X, 6:55 "that the way become clear", 37:117 "the lucid Book"), mubayyinah (II, 4:19/65:1/33:30 a "manifest" indecency = distinctly evident). The two faces are not two roots: 2:187 welds them — "until the white thread becomes DISTINCT (yatabayyana) to you FROM (min) the black thread", and the same verse closes "thus God makes-distinct (yubayyinu) His signs." 2:256 repeats it: "right conduct has become DISTINCT (tabayyana) FROM (min) error." Manifestness in this root is always distinctness-against-a-background, i.e. the same demarcation seen from its epistemic side.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM carries voice/aspect, not the residue. Form II (bayyana) = causative "cause to be set-apart / made distinct" (explain); the -in ending of mubin is the Form IV active participle "one that makes/stands distinct"; Form V (tabayyana) = reflexive/mediopassive "come to be distinct" or, in imperative with human agent (49:6 fatabayyanu, 4:94), "seek the distinction / ascertain"; Forms X (istabana, mustabin) add the seeking/emergent nuance. CONSTRUCTION carries the dyad: LOC bayna is a bound locative taking two complements (…wa…, or a plural/dual) — it grammaticalizes the "two poles" the root demands. bayna yadayhi is a frozen construction ("before / in the presence of / preceding"), but the residue "the interval in front of two hands" survives. CONTEXT supplies WHAT is separated (thread from thread, truth from error, one party from another, heaven-earth, two seas) and WHAT is made evident (signs, proof, an indecency, a way). Subtracting all three, the invariant left in every occurrence is: an interval/boundary between two, and/or the distinctness of one set apart from another.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The most bleached uses are the pure locative prepositions — ma baynahuma "what is between them" (15:85), bayna yadayhi "before it/him" (10:37, 13:11), bayna dhalika "between that" (17:110). Here almost nothing but the bare "interval between two" survives; the "distinctness/clarity" face is dormant. This is not a defeater, because the separation face IS the root residue (its other pole), and these uses never denote anything but the demarcating interval — they never drift to an unrelated sense. A second potential resister, tabayyana meaning "verify/ascertain" (49:6, 4:94), is reconciled: to ascertain is to seek the distinction of true from false — the make-distinct residue in an epistemic-imperative construction, confirmed by 2:256/2:187 where tabayyana + min is literally "become distinct from."
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Homonymy: that b-y-n is really two accidentally-similar roots — one meaning "separation/between" (bayn, baynahum) and one meaning "clarity/manifestation" (bayyin, mubin, bayyinah) — so no single contribution is universally present; each cluster simply has its own sense. This is the strongest rival because the LOC pole (interval) and the mubin pole (manifestness) feel semantically far apart, and a reader could treat "between" as a mere function word unrelated to "clear."
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Against homonymy, the packet's own bridge occurrences fuse the two poles inside single verses: 2:187 "yatabayyanu … al-khaytu al-abyadu MIN al-khayti al-aswad" and 2:256 "tabayyana al-rushdu MIN al-ghayy" express clarity as literal separation-from, and 2:187 pairs tabayyana with yubayyinu in one breath. So the internal evidence unifies rather than splits. Against nearest roots: f-r-q (farq) = breaking a unity into scattered parts; f-s-l (fasl) = sectioning/decisive judgment by jointing; z-y-l (10:28 zayyala) = removal/parting. None of these yields "clear/manifest/evident." b-y-n is distinctively DYADIC (an interval between exactly-related poles, not a shattering into many) and uniquely spans to epistemic distinctness (a thing set apart = evident). That span — demarcation that becomes manifestness — is the falsifiable, non-empty residue no neighbor shares.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 523 occurrences are accounted for by cluster, with every singleton form (V-IV 43:52, V-X 6:55, ADJ-X 37:117, N-II 33:30, ADJ-II 4:19/65:1) directly inspected, plus a broad direct read across LOC, N, N(IV), ADJ(IV), V(II), V(V). A single residue — demarcation-between yielding distinctness — is demonstrably present in each: the LOC cluster instantiates the separating-interval face, the clarity cluster the distinctness/manifestness face, and internal bridge verses (2:187, 2:256) prove these are one notion, not two roots. The residue is non-empty, falsifiable, and distinctive against f-r-q / f-s-l / z-y-l (dyadic interval + epistemic manifestness, which none of them carry). Strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG for two honest reasons: (1) the residue is genuinely two-poled and the bleached prepositional bayna foregrounds only the separation face, so the unity rests on an abstraction ("demarcation → distinctness") rather than on a surface sense visible in every token; (2) that abstraction, while internally corroborated, is doing real interpretive work to hold the poles together. No occurrence resists, so universal presence holds; result PREFERRED.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Full coverage assessed by cluster across all 523 occurrences (LOC 243 "bayna" = interval/face-a; mubin/bayyina N,N(IV),ADJ ~224 = manifestness/face-b; V(II) bayyana / V(V) tabayyana / V(X) istabana / ADJ(X) mustabin ~56 = make/become distinct/face-b). The DISJUNCTIVE core (separating-interval OR resulting-distinctness) is demonstrably present in EVERY confirmed occurrence — no occurrence lacks both faces — and several verses show both faces jointly (2:256 tabayyana al-rushd MIN al-ghayy; 2:187 white thread distinct FROM black; 16:103 arabiyy mubin vs a'jami). So the residue is non-empty and universally realized in its disjunctive form.

Why NOT SUPPORTED: the proposal bundles two extra descriptors that fail universal presence. (1) "Inherently dyadic (A demarcated from/against B)" is not demonstrably present in the monadic manifestness cases where mubin predicates a single referent's clarity with no second referent and no spatial interval: 10:76/11:7 (sihr mubin), 11:6/12:1/15:1 (kitab/qur'an mubin), 11:25/15:89 (nadhir mubin), 15:18 (shihab mubin), 15:79 (imam mubin), 16:35/16:82 (al-balagh al-mubin), 43:52 (yubin = articulate speech). Dyadicity there survives only by positing an implicit background B, which is an unfalsifiable rescue. (2) "Two CO-present faces" (both active each time) is false for pure-LOC "between" (no manifestness) and pure-predicate mubin (no interval); the faces are alternately, not jointly, realized. Under non-negotiable unity a stated component not present in confirmed occurrences means verdict != SUPPORTED.

Distinctiveness: the interval "between" sense is uniquely distinctive (no rival root), so distinctiveness_ok=true overall; however the separation/distinctness face overlaps materially with f-r-q and f-S-l — the packet itself co-locates them (2:136 la nufarriqu BAYNA; 18:78 firaq BAYNI; 6:55 nufaSSil...tastabin; 2:185 al-furqan beside bayyinat) — and the manifestness face overlaps with Z-h-r/j-l-w. This weakens distinctiveness on face-b specifically.

Falsifiable: the core universal claim (every occurrence shows demarcation/distinctness) is a strong, testable, falsifiable-in-principle prediction (falsifiable=true); but the "inherently dyadic + two-faced" formulation reduces PRACTICAL falsifiability because any counterexample can be absorbed by assigning the other face or positing an implicit B. Recommendation: drop "inherently dyadic" and "co-present" as universal descriptors; state the residue as a single disjunctive contribution (interval-that-sets-apart, yielding distinctness), which then holds across all 523 occurrences.
